title: Enrolment at Polyclinics for Healthier SG
what_it_is: Enrolment at Polyclinics for Healthier SG

sections.label: Polyclinic and GP enrolment capacity
sections.summary: Average polyclinic enrolment capacity is near 30,000, 19 of 25 polyclinics have spare capacity, and Healthier SG GP clinics can enrol over 700,000 residents.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The average enrolment capacity is close to 30,000 per polyclinic.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Of the 25 polyclinics, 19 polyclinics still have spare capacity to take in more enrolees; while six are reserving their capacities for their regular chronic patients to enrol, before deciding if they could take in non-regular or new residents.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: A key design feature of Healthier SG is to extend the benefits of fully-subsidised preventative check-ins, health screening and vaccinations and chronic drug subsidies to private clinics.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: There is currently capacity at Healthier SG GP clinics to enrol more than 700,000 residents.

sections.label: Polyclinic versus GP enrolment demand
sections.summary: 65% of enrolees are with Healthier SG GP clinics; among polyclinic enrolees, 81% are existing regular patients and 19% are non-regular or new.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: For the first one, in terms of the relative demand, for enrolment at polyclinic versus a GP, 65% of the total that have enrolled, are enrolled with a Healthier SG GP clinic.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Among the polyclinic enrolees, 81% are existing regular patients, while the remaining 19% are non-regular and new patients.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Of the regular polyclinic patients, about 26% have enrolled with a GP clinic.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: To Member's second question, the short answer would be, no.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, it depends on what it is they are a regular patient for: do they have a chronic disease that falls under the Healthier SG programme; are they regular for a short period of time or have they been a regular patient over a longer period of time?

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, if you take it in the spirit that the polyclinics would like to continue to serve those patients who have chronic diseases; which they have been following up and which Healthier SG would be able to assist them, then the answer is, yes.
